key_insight: PointDiT shows that monocular 3D geometry estimation can be done effectively with a simple pixel-space diffusion transformer, without relying on heavy hybrid architectures or latent-space compression. By operating directly on raw 3D point map patches and conditioning on image tokens, it simplifies the pipeline while preserving strong reconstruction performance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the complexity and fragility of existing single-image 3D reconstruction methods, which often depend on elaborate architectures, hand-crafted loss combinations, or latent diffusion setups that compress geometry and add overhead.
method: Use a plain Vision Transformer as a diffusion model directly in pixel space.
Predict raw 3D point map patches instead of encoding geometry into a latent representation.
Condition the diffusion process on image tokens from a pretrained image encoder to guide reconstruction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that high-quality monocular geometry estimation may not require complicated system design. The approach lowers architectural complexity and can make 3D reconstruction pipelines easier to build, train, and adapt.

paper_title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
paper_authors: Haofei Xu, Rundi Wu, Philipp Henzler, Nikolai Kalischek, Michael Oechsle
